text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak and French President Chirac discuss in Cairo today Chirac's tour in the region and bilateral ties. Foreign Minister Moussa: I expect fruitful discussions from the two leaders on how to save the peace process. Chirac tells Jordan's parliament: peace is in danger and strength will not guarantee the security of any country in the region. France suggests establishing a permanent office for a European peace envoy in Cairo or Damascus.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says Egypt is equipped to take on a fundamental role in spearheading regional cooperation. Egyptian working group proposes 130 regional projects, including 66 industrial projects, to be discussed at the Middle East economic summit.
- Egypt to plant 921,000 acres of cotton this year, 211,000 acres more than last year. Average production of each acre is 8.7 qantars (870 lb), a historic high.
- Mubarak and Chirac to save the peace process in their talks today. Moussa says Egypt appreciates Chirac's balanced position and European cooperation is necessary.

- Oil Minister Banbi says Egypt is one of the world's most important countries for foreign companies seeking crude and natural gas. He also says there are 48 international firms working on concessions in Egypt.
- Ganzouri and the summit committee decide on the final preparations for the Cairo economic summit. Egypt will link approval for any new projects to their ability to create jobs.
- An overall plan to raise Egypt's exports to Germany. Potatoes, cotton, fruits and vegetables are on the list. Germany grants Egypt 133 million pounds.
- Sudanese newspaper affirms Khartoum's absolute need for Egypt.
- Chirac: Egypt must remain powerful and leading in the region.
- Defence Minister Tantawi: Egypt is living through a golden age of affecting regional and international politics.
- Cotton production is more than enough to cover local demand and Egypt can export 1.5 to 2.0 million qantars.
